Pale runway, dry yellow-brown grass, leafless trees and distant vehicles sit beneath pale blue sky. Match the reference photograph: pointed nose with slender test probe, dark canopy, side intakes, swept wings, two outward-canted tail fins, one rear exhaust, small forward-fuselage flags and historical markings. Keep authentic F-35A proportions, not a sci-fi jet. Chief pilot Jon Beesley is only an indistinct silhouette. Nose raised, nose gear and both main gear assemblies extended, light struts and dark tires. A calm adult English narrator with a measured documentary delivery says exactly: “The F-35A has one engine.” 5–8 s: Continue tracking the same AA-1 flying in a shallow climb, gear still extended. Replace the fact label with “Conventional takeoff” lower left. The same narrator says exactly: “It takes off from a conventional runway.” Finish speech before the end. Natural single-engine jet roar stays beneath the voice. This is an excerpt of the inaugural development flight, not the entire sortie. No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.

research.subject: The F-35A Lightning II’s first flight: prototype AA-1 taking off at Fort Worth, Texas, on December 15, 2006. For the eight-second film, show runway acceleration and liftoff, then an airborne view. Keep 'F-35A Lightning II' visible; introduce 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' in turn. Suggested calm English narration: 'The F-35A Lightning II. One engine. Conventional takeoff from a runway.'

looks.thing: F-35A prototype AA-1 — exterior at first liftoff
looks.look: The December 15, 2006 photograph documents a gray aircraft with an angular pointed nose, dark canopy, swept wings, two outward-canted tail fins, and side air intakes. Small national flags and 'F-35 LIGHTNING II' lettering appear on the forward fuselage. A slender test probe projects ahead of the nose. These are visible photographic details, not invented additions. ([d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net](https://d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net/thumbs/photos/2507/9159911/1000w_q95.jpg))

The Air Force specification lists a length of 51 feet, wingspan of 35 feet, and height of 14 feet. Use these published F-35A dimensions as a general proportion check, while matching the historical AA-1 photograph for episode-specific geometry and markings; the fact sheet is not an AA-1-specific dimensional drawing. ([af.mil](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/478441/f-35a-lightning-ii-conventional-takeoff-and-landing-variant/sf2589626/f-35a-lightning-ii/?utm_source=openai))

The historical photograph shows the aircraft just above the runway, nose raised, with its nose gear and both main landing-gear assemblies extended. The exposed struts are light-colored and the tires dark. This is the documented posture to match for the liftoff shot. ([d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net](https://d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net/thumbs/photos/2507/9159911/1000w_q95.jpg))

The photograph shows a broad, pale paved runway bordered by dry yellow-brown grass. Behind it are leafless trees, distant vehicles on a low rise, and a pale blue sky. No prominent building is needed to reproduce this documented composition. ([d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net](https://d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net/thumbs/photos/2507/9159911/1000w_q95.jpg))

looks.thing: Chief pilot Jon Beesley — cockpit occupant
looks.look: The takeoff photograph shows only a small, dark pilot silhouette beneath the canopy. It does not establish facial appearance, clothing details, or age. Keep the pilot indistinct rather than inventing a close-up or unsupported flight equipment. Beesley’s identity as the pilot is established by the first-flight reporting. ([d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net](https://d1ldvf68ux039x.cloudfront.net/thumbs/photos/2507/9159911/1000w_q95.jpg))

facts.fact: The aircraft was AA-1, the first prototype F-35A Lightning II, and its December 15, 2006 sortie was the F-35’s first flight. The Joint Program Office identifies the aircraft and episode in its historical account. ([jsf.mil](https://www.jsf.mil/NewsArticle/276?utm_source=openai))

Lockheed Martin chief pilot Jon Beesley flew the inaugural sortie. He reported afterward that the aircraft had performed well. ([investors.lockheedmartin.com](https://investors.lockheedmartin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lockheed-martin-f-35-lightning-ii-stealth-fighter-completes/?utm_source=openai))

Takeoff occurred at 12:44 p.m. Central Standard Time at Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas. An official photograph records the aircraft lifting away from the runway with its landing gear extended. ([af.mil](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/128701/engineers-contribute-to-f-35-initial-flight-success/?utm_source=openai))
facts.when: December 15, 2006; Air Force report published December 16, 2006.

facts.fact: The F-35A is the conventional takeoff and landing variant, intended to operate from traditional airstrips. 'Conventional takeoff' is therefore an accurate on-screen label for this runway departure. ([jsf.mil](https://www.jsf.mil/NewsArticle/276?utm_source=openai))
facts.when: December 15, 2006 episode; variant description published December 15, 2022.

facts.fact: The F-35A has one engine: the Air Force lists one Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100 turbofan. The contemporary first-flight release identifies the inaugural aircraft’s engine as a Pratt & Whitney F135. 'One engine' is accurate. ([af.mil](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/478441/f-35a-lightning-ii-conventional-takeoff-and-landing-variant/sf2589626/f-35a-lightning-ii/?utm_source=openai))
facts.when: First flight: December 15, 2006; Air Force specification marked current as of April 2014.

facts.fact: After departure, the aircraft climbed to 15,000 feet. The pilot performed maneuvers to evaluate handling and the operation of the engine and aircraft subsystems: this was a development test flight, not a combat mission. ([af.mil](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/128701/engineers-contribute-to-f-35-initial-flight-success/?utm_source=openai))

The aircraft returned to land at 1:19 p.m. Central Standard Time, 35 minutes after departure. The eight-second film should depict an excerpt of takeoff and flight, not imply that the entire sortie lasted eight seconds. ([af.mil](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/128701/engineers-contribute-to-f-35-initial-flight-success/?utm_source=openai))

The successful inaugural flight began the F-35 flight-test campaign. At the time, Lockheed Martin described a planned 12,000-hour program intended to validate extensive laboratory testing; that figure was a program plan, not hours already flown. ([investors.lockheedmartin.com](https://investors.lockheedmartin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lockheed-martin-f-35-lightning-ii-stealth-fighter-completes/?utm_source=openai))

story.style: Live-action widescreen documentary realism; steady tracking views, natural daylight, and AA-1’s documented proportions, geometry and markings.
story.story:
In the opening two seconds, a widescreen live-action view shows AA-1, the first F-35A Lightning II prototype, lifting off at Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, at 12:44 p.m. Central Standard Time on December 15, 2006. The title reads “F-35A Lightning II.” Chief pilot Jon Beesley remains an indistinct silhouette beneath the dark canopy.

The gray aircraft rises nose-high above the pale runway, with its nose gear and both main landing-gear assemblies extended. Its pointed nose, slender test probe, swept wings, side intakes and two outward-canted tail fins match the documented aircraft. From seconds two through five, “One engine” appears; calm English narration says, “The F-35A has one engine.”

From seconds five through eight, the view follows AA-1 flying after departure. “Conventional takeoff” replaces the previous fact label, while the narrator says, “It takes off from a conventional runway.” These successive views show an excerpt of the inaugural development test flight, not its full thirty-five-minute duration.
story.title: F-35A Lightning II — First Flight
